key_insight: SurgFormer is a multiresolution gated transformer that learns to predict nodewise soft-tissue deformations on volumetric meshes from solver-generated data, enabling near real-time, scalable simulation with explicit support for tissue resection.
problem_solved: High-fidelity biomechanical solvers are too slow for interactive surgical use; SurgFormer provides fast, accurate deformation predictions on complex volumetric meshes while handling topology changes from resections.
method: Build a fixed mesh hierarchy and process geometry with repeated multibranch blocks.
Each block fuses local message passing (for short-range interactions), coarse global self-attention (for long-range context), and pointwise feedforward updates via gated transformers.
Train on high-fidelity solver outputs to predict nodewise displacement fields and run inference in near real-time, including resection events.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable architecture for real-time soft-tissue simulation that ML practitioners can adapt for surgical planning, interactive training, and downstream control tasks where speed and handling of topology changes are critical.

paper_title: SurgFormer: Scalable Learning of Organ Deformation with Resection Support and Real-Time Inference
paper_authors: Ashkan Shahbazi, Elaheh Akbari, Kyvia Pereira, Jon S. Heiselman, Annie C. Benson
